text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- IMPORTS ARE RISING
The government is expected to unveil the 15th trade deficit in the 28 months of its Real economic stabilization plan, with imports seen outstripping exports by $900 million in October.
-- LONG-TERM INTEREST RATE TO FALL TO 11 PCT AS OF DEC
As of December, the long-term interest rate (TJLP) will fall 25 percent to around 11 percent a year from 14.97 percent previously.
O GLOBO
-- SHOOTING AND BOMBS AT DAWN IN COPACABANA
Residents in Rio's Copacabana neighborhood were subjected to five hours of gun battles between drug traffickers in nearby shanty towns.
-- DULL DEBATE UNLIKELY TO CHANGE ELECTION TREND
A television debate between Rio's two mayoral candidates, Sergio Cabral and Luiz Paulo Conde, is unlikely to change the election trend as Cabral failed to unsettle Conde who is leading in the polls.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SAVINGS FROM REDUNDANCIES SEEN AT 40 MLN REAIS
The government hopes to save 40 million reais a month by cutting jobs with its voluntary redundancy program.
-- INFLATION BACK ON THE RISE IN SAO PAULO IN NOV
Sao Paulo inflation is inching back up in November, measuring 0.78 percent in the four weeks to November 7, up from 0.58 in the previous four-week period.
-- PITTA STABLE AT 55 PCT AND ERUNDINA AT 34 PCT
Sao Paulo mayoral candidate Celso Pitta remains stable in the polls at 55 percent of the vote, compared with 34 percent for his opponent Luiza Erundina.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
